description: US/CA-only refactor deny-list (docs/refactor-plan.md Phase 10): removed markets, data sources, and symbols that must not reappear in shipped code. Matched case-insensitively as substrings, scoped to agent/src, agent/backtest, and frontend/src. Intentional mentions belong in `allow` below, each with a non-empty reason; an allow entry suppresses exactly the listed tokens for the matching path (repo-relative path or fnmatch glob). agent/tests/test_us_ca_scope_gate.py enforces both the deny-list and the allowlist's honesty (every entry must carry a reason and must still suppress a real hit). Phase 11 token-spelling note: the matcher is a case-insensitive SUBSTRING search, so short exchange suffixes and currency codes cannot be added bare. Measured collisions in the scan roots at Phase 11: nse 2131 hits (response/sense/expense), bse 1088, hose 533 (those/whose/chose), lse 4987 (false/else/pulse), .BO 127 (".bold"/".bootstrap"/".body"), .BA 473 (".back"/".base"), .SS 25 (".ssl"/".sse"), .SH 398 (".sh"/".sha256"), .L 2665, ARS 2794 (years/args), and HKD/CNY/GBP/INR/JPY/KRW/VND all collide with the surviving multi-currency portfolio/FX tables (portfolio/service.py, portfolio/iso4217.py, market_data.py). Those bare forms are therefore omitted. Exchange suffixes are an exception: in code a suffix can only be a string literal (a comment cannot route a market), so the suffix tokens below carry their CLOSING double quote - '.SS"' matches ".SS" in a suffix table, endswith(".SS") and f"{code}.SS", but never '.ssl'/'.sse'. '.SH"' is the one suffix that still collides (file-extension lists like ".sh") and '.HK"' still matches surviving portfolio HK-journal handling, so both are omitted and the exact symbols stay as guards. crypto/forex/futures stay untokened for the same reason: crypto is a surviving Robinhood instrument class and MARKET_SPECS market, while forex/futures appear in generic prose and surviving symbol classification. Longer multi-word venue names (hong kong, shanghai, shenzhen, buenos aires) plus kospi/kosdaq are specific enough to include; their surviving prose mentions are allowlisted below.
